subject: Implementation ops and vector DB tradeoffs for embeddings+rerank
messages:
From: Samantha Klein <samantha.k@acme.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Gonzalez <matt.gonzalez@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff -- index size / backfill Qs

Hi Laura / Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the search team at Acme is excited to move from proof-of-concept to a phased rollout. Before we lock in timelines, two quick questions that will affect our migration approach and cost model: 

1) Index sizing: we expect ~375M documents (log lines + product metadata), but many will be short. Any guidance on realistic vector store sizing assumptions you recommend for estimating HB storage and backfill throughput?

2) Rerank evals: we plan to run an internal offline rerank evaluation against a 50k sample. Should we use your hosted embeddings or generate locally and upload vectors? Concerns: ensuring identical tokenization/encoder, and avoiding double-embedding costs.

I attached an export with current doc counts/approx sizes (acme_index_estimate.csv). Can someone from the implementation team advise on tradeoffs so we can finalize the SOW?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Klein
Director, Search Infrastructure
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_index_estimate.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Klein <samantha.k@acme.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff -- index size / backfill Qs

Hi Samantha — thanks for sharing the estimate. Looping in Marissa (CSM) and Ben (solutions) to weigh in. High-level thoughts below, followed by proposed next steps.

Quick guidance on sizing and approach:
- Vector store sizing: our rule-of-thumb for short text (avg 25-40 tokens) is ~1.8-2.2 bytes per token after float16/quantization and store metadata; for 375M docs we usually see vector storage in the low-to-mid TBs if you use 1536-d embeddings with PQ/quantization profiles. We’ll run a quick sample calculation once we validate the token distribution.
- Backfill throughput: with Dedicated capacity (2x A100-like nodes + batchers) we can sustain ~50-70k vectors/minute for bulk import if network/IO are healthy. If you’re on hosted, expect lower sustained throughput; we can propose a mixed approach (local seed + hosted completion).

Rerank eval approach options (pros/cons):
- Hosted embeddings (Redwood API): simplest for parity with serving — ensures same tokenizer/encoder and avoids drift. Cost shows up on our billing; you can offset with a short credit runway for eval.
- Local generation & upload: lower immediate API spend but risk of mismatch (esp. if you run different tokenizers). Also adds complexity for vector normalization and metadata hygiene.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to propose an implementation cadence and decide whether to seed with a staged backfill or do a single cutover (see playbook).
2) Ben to validate sample export for token distribution and produce an updated sizing calc.
3) If Acme prefers hosted embeddings for rerank evals, we can arrange a short promotional credit and dedicated throughput window.

I’ll attach the migration playbook for your review; Marissa will coordinate the kickoff dates.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_migration_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 480KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Klein <samantha.k@acme.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff -- index size / backfill Qs

Hi Samantha — looping in the implementation plan below and a short checklist so we can converge on dates. I’ll run the kickoff once we have internal signoff.

Implementation checklist (recommended phased rollout):
- Phase 0: Sampling & baseline
  - Ben will run tokenization analysis on the attached CSV sample and return avg tokens/document + estimated vector count. (ETA: 48 hours)
  - Create a 50k representative sample for offline rerank tests (we recommend stratified sampling across doc types).
- Phase 1: Seed indexing (non-prod)
  - Upload 10% of corpus to a staging vector store; validate retrieval latency and rerank precision metrics.
  - Run rerank evals using Redwood-hosted embeddings to avoid embedding drift.
- Phase 2: Controlled backfill
  - Backfill remaining corpus in 3 windows, monitor ingestion throughput and query SLAs.
  - Canary traffic routing to new rerank path for 1% of queries for 48 hours.
- Phase 3: Cutover & post-cutover verification
  - Final sync, promote index, and monitor metrics for 7 days.

Operational decisions we need from Acme now:
- Preferred vector store: Self-hosted (we recommend Milvus/FAISS on k8s) or managed (we can coordinate with Pinecone/Weaviate if you prefer). If you pick managed, confirm retention/replication requirements.
- Rerank eval run: Hosted embeddings (recommended) or local (customer-managed).

Please confirm preferred vector store and whether you want Redwood to run hosted embeddings for the eval. Once confirmed I’ll schedule Ben’s tokenization run and lock the kickoff window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

- Rerank eval: yes, please run hosted embeddings for the 50k offline eval. Please use the same model we demonstrated (redwood-embed-1536-v2).
- Kickoff: target week of Oct 18 for Phase 0 sampling; we’ll provide a 50k sample export by Oct 11.

Marissa — once Ben returns the tokenization numbers we’ll sign the SOW and route procurement. We can put a small eval credit on the hosted embedding runs if needed.

Matt
